**Tsukiyomi-no-miya** (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ar|إيسه|azb|ایسه، میه|bcl|Ise, Mie|be|Ісэ (горад)|ca|Ise (ciutat japonesa)|ce|Исе (гӀала)|ckb|ئیسێ|cs|Ise (Mie)|de|Ise (Mie)|eo|Ise (urbo)|es|Ise (Mie)|et|Ise (Jaapan)|eu|Ise (Mie)|fa|ایسه، میه|fi|Ise (kaupunki)|fr|Ise (Mie)|gl|Ise|hr|Ise|hy|Իսե (քաղաք)|id|Ise, Mie|it|Ise (Giappone)|ja|伊勢市|ka|ისე|ko|이세시|lt|Isė (Japonija)|mg|Ise|mzn|ایسه، میه|nl|Ise (Mie)|no|Ise (Mie)|pl|Ise (Japonia)|pt|Ise (Japão)|ro|Ise, Japonia|ru|Исе (город)|sh|Ise|simple|Ise, Mie|sr|Исе|sv|Ise, Japan|szl|Ise (Japůńijo)|tg|Исе|tl|Ise, Mie|tr|Ise (şehir)|tt|Исе (шәħәр)|uk|Ісе (Міє)|ur|ایسے، میہ|uz|Ise (Mie)|vi|Ise, Mie|war|Ise, Mie|zh|伊勢市|zh_classical|伊勢市|zh_min_nan|Ise-chhī|zh_yue|伊勢|qid=Q328067}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}.<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 16</ref> It is a betsugu (auxiliary shrine) of the Outer Shrine (Gekū), {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343}}, of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} complex.<ref name="tm" /><ref name="ik">Ise Bunkasha, ed. (2008): p. 39</ref><ref name="mr">Mirai Publishing (2013): p. 64</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 69</ref><ref name="rg">JTB Publishing (2011): p. 42</ref><ref name="rb">Publishing Business Headquarters, Domestic Information Dept., Third Editorial Dept., ed. (2014): p. 34</ref><ref name="as">Mitsuhashi (2013): p. 124</ref> It is also a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}.

== Overview ==
[[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]]

Tsukiyomi-no-miya is a betsugu of the Outer Shrine located about 300 m north of the Gekū and about 500 m west of {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise City Station}}. Two deities—{{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto}} and his aramitama (rough/active spirit), Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama—are enshrined together in the same shrine building.<ref name="mr" /><ref name="rg" />

At {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naikū)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}}, a betsugu of the Inner Shrine, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto and his aramitama are enshrined in separate buildings. By contrast, at Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月夜見宮) they are enshrined together in a single structure, which is a distinguishing feature.<ref name="rb" /> The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮|qid=Q11665463}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya|qid=Q11665488}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命).

Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts.<ref name="mr" /><ref name="rg" /><ref name="as" /> Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere.<ref name="mr" /><ref name="rg" /> The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)}}.<ref name="ik" /><ref name="gk" />

The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 37|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357923}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the '''Hatsuhobiki''' (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine.

Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|qid=Q17225931}}.<ref name="ik" /> To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari Ōkami|ja|稲荷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q719665}} shrine,<ref name="tm" /> and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers.<ref name="rg" /> Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a '''Shukueiya''' (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌).

A narrow, 4-meter-wide straight path known as '''Kamiji Street''' (神路通り, "Path of the Gods") connects the North Gate (北御門, Kita-mikado) of the Outer Shrine to Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and is believed to be the route taken by deities. See {{ill|Kamiji Street|ja|神路通り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiji Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30114580}} for details.

== History ==
Its origins are not certain, but it is said that in ancient times it was called '''Takagawara''' and was a shrine that enshrined an agricultural deity. In the *Engishiki* compiled in 927 (the 5th year of Engi) during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}}, it was ranked first among the Outer Shrine's sessha. In the *Toyuke-no-miya Gishikichō* it is recorded as "Tsukuyomi Shrine," in the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō* as "Tsukiyomi Shrine," and in the *Ise Daijingū Shiki* as "Tsukiyomi Sha."<ref name="as" /> In 1210 (the 4th year of Jōgen), it was elevated to the status of a betsugu.<ref name="gk" /><ref name="as2">Mitsuhashi (2013): p. 125</ref>

In the Meiji period, the Outer Shrine betsugu came to be written as '''月夜見宮''', while the Inner Shrine betsugu came to be written as '''月讀宮'''.<ref name="tm" /> During the {{ill|Ise Riot|Q11379085|qid=Q11379085}} of 1876 (Meiji 9), nearby towns burned and, out of concern that fire might spread to Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the sacred object ({{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}) was temporarily moved to {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|Q11665463|qid=Q11665463}}.<ref>Kaneko (1983): p. 214</ref> During the {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}}, the {{ill|Ujiyamada Air Raid|Q18990749|qid=Q18990749}} occurred on July 29, 1945. Although all surrounding houses burned down, due to desperate firefighting and a fortunate failure of an incendiary bomb lodged in the thatched roof to explode, only the shrine buildings of Tsukiyomi-no-miya remained standing amid the ruins.<ref>Yano (2006): pp. 184–185</ref>

== Festivals ==
The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ar|البيت الإمبراطوري في اليابان|as|জাপানৰ ৰাজপৰিয়াল|ast|Familia imperial xaponesa|az|Yaponiya imperator evi|be|Імператарскі дом Японіі|ca|Família Imperial del Japó|ckb|خێزانی شاھانەی ژاپۆن|cs|Japonská císařská dynastie|de|Japanisches Kaiserhaus|el|Αυτοκρατορικός Οίκος της Ιαπωνίας|eo|Japana reĝa familio|es|Familia imperial japonesa|fa|دودمان یاماتو|fr|Maison impériale du Japon|he|בית הקיסרות של יפן|hr|Japanska carska obitelj|hu|Japán császári ház|id|Wangsa Kekaisaran Jepang|it|Famiglia imperiale del Giappone|ja|皇室|ko|일본 황실|la|Domus imperatoriae Iaponiae|ms|Kerabat diraja Jepun|no|Japans keiserhus|pt|Casa Imperial do Japão|ro|Familia imperială a Japoniei|ru|Японский императорский дом|sh|Carska kuća Japana|simple|Imperial House of Japan|sq|Shtëpia Perandorake e Japonisë|th|ราชวงศ์ญี่ปุ่น|tr|Yamato Hanedanı|uk|Імператорський дім Японії|ur|جاپان کا شاہی خاندان|vi|Hoàng thất Nhật Bản|zh|日本皇室|zh_classical|日本皇室|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún hông-sek|zh_yue|日本皇室|qid=Q909452|lt=Imperial House of Japan}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}* and *{{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}}*).

* '''January'''
** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}} (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|qid=Q2150|lt=January 1}}
*** A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage.
** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|en|January 3|qid=Q2156|lt=January 3}}
*** A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule.

* '''February'''
** {{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭}} (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|en|February 11|qid=Q2335|lt=February 11}}
*** Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}.
** {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}} (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|en|February 18|qid=Q2343|lt=February 18}}
*** A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace.
** {{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|en|February 23|qid=Q2352|lt=February 23}}
*** A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Naruhito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳仁|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q217096}}.

* '''May'''
** {{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|en|May 14|qid=Q2561|lt=May 14}}
*** Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest.

* '''June'''
** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}} (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|en|June 18|qid=Q2670|lt=June 18}}–{{ill|June 19|en|June 19|qid=Q2669|lt=June 19}}
*** A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭).

* '''August'''
** {{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|en|August 4|qid=Q2784|lt=August 4}}
*** A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity.

* '''October'''
** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|en|October 18|qid=Q2964|lt=October 18}}–{{ill|October 19|en|October 19|qid=Q2961|lt=October 19}}
*** A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods.

* '''November'''
** {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}} (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|en|November 24|qid=Q3022|lt=November 24}}
*** A festival in which the emperor offers the season's first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude.

* '''December'''
** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}} (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|en|December 18|qid=Q2438|lt=December 18}}–{{ill|December 19|en|December 19|qid=Q2451|lt=December 19}}

* {{ill|October 5|en|October 5|qid=Q2930|lt=October 5}} – {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|檐付祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nokitsukesai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}} (Eaves-Attaching Festival)
* {{ill|November 5|en|November 5|qid=Q2993|lt=November 5}} – {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|甍祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irakasai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}} (Roofing Festival)

'''2015'''
* {{ill|February 26|en|February 26|qid=Q2359|lt=February 26}} – {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|御戸祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitosai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}} / Mifunashiro Hōnōshiki / Araikiyome
* {{ill|February 27|en|February 27|qid=Q2361|lt=February 27}} – {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|杵築祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotsukisai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}} / {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|後鎮祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gochinsai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}} / {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|川原大祓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawahara Ōharai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}}
* {{ill|February 28|en|February 28|qid=Q2362|lt=February 28}} – {{ill|Okazari|ja|御飾}} / {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}} (Transfer of the deity)
* {{ill|March 1|en|March 1|qid=Q2393|lt=March 1}} – {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌}} / {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}}

Among these, the Ritchūsai, Jōtōsai, Kotsukisai, Gochinsai, Sengyo, and Hōhei are conducted according to dates determined by imperial decision.<ref name="sg" /> In addition, on {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|qid=Q2351|lt=February 22}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishimochi|ja|お白石持|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshiraishi-mochi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17225061}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the Miyago offering group carried sacred white stones in carts from the Uraguchi intersection to Tsukiyomi-no-miya, covering a distance of 1.2 km.<ref name="cn1502">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title="Enya" linking to the next generation: Oshiraishi-mochi event at Tsukiyomi-no-miya in Ise|author=Yudai Nakahira|publisher=Chunichi Shimbun|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}</ref> With this, all oshiraishi-mochi events for the betsugu were completed.<ref name="cn1502" />

=== Precincts ===
* '''Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月夜見宮)''' — A Betsugū (auxiliary shrine) of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}). In keeping with the Outer Shrine, the thatched shinmei-zukuri building faces south and has outward-cut chigi and five (an odd number) katsuogi. The old site for relocation (kodenchi) lies adjacent east–west. A relocation ({{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|Q3959472|qid=Q3959472}}) is performed once every 20 years. There is a tradition that when people of Miyago pulled the sacred construction timber (役木) and reached Yōkaichiba-chō, a fire broke out in Miyago, and the pullers returned to fight it; the people of Yōkaichiba-chō took over pulling the timber, and ever since, at the *{{ill|Okihiki|Q11489125|qid=Q11489125}}* the people of Yōkaichiba-chō have pulled and offered the timber to Tsukiyomi-no-miya.
* '''{{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|qid=Q17225931}}''' — Dedicated to the mitama (spirit) of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto. Located within the precincts of Tsukiyomi-no-miya, but it is a sessha of Toyouke Daijingu (the Outer Shrine).
* '''{{ill|Inari shrine|fa|معبد ایناری|fr|Sanctuaire Inari|ja|稲荷神社|ko|이나리 신사|simple|Inari shrine|uk|Святилище Інарі|qid=Q514480}}''' — A shrine dedicated to Inari, the deity of prosperity and agriculture.
* '''Shukueiya (宿衛屋)''' — A guardhouse for shrine officials.

=== Kamiji Street ===
[[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|Kamiji Street]]
The straight road about 4 m wide running from the Outer Shrine's Kita-mikado (North Gate) to Tsukiyomi-no-miya is regarded as "the road the gods pass," and is called '''Kamiji Street''' (神路通り). See the article {{ill|Kamiji Street|Q30114580|qid=Q30114580}}.

=== Devotee organization ===
In 1960 (Shōwa 35), a Tsukiyomi confraternity (Tsukiyomi-kō) was formed mainly by worshippers living in Ise, later renamed the Tsukiyomi-no-miya Hōsankai. The Hōsankai carries out activities such as holding a festival of gratitude for divine blessings on April 19 and September 19 each year.

=== Access ===
* About a 10-minute walk from {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشン|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise City Station}} on the JR {{ill|Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023}} and the Kintetsu {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line}}.<ref name="tm" /><ref name="rb" />
* About a 5-minute walk from the Outer Shrine Kita-mikado entrance via {{ill|Kamiji Street|Q30114580|qid=Q30114580}}.<ref name="mr" /><ref name="rg2">JTB Publishing (2011): p. 43</ref>
* About a 3-minute walk from the Shindō bus stop (Mie Kōtsū {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516}}), and immediately from the "Tsukiyomi-no-miya-mae" stop on the Ise City community bus {{ill|Q11379021|ja|伊勢市コミュニティバス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Community Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379021}}.
* About 3 km from the {{ill|Ise interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884857}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|Q6079578|qid=Q6079578}}.
* Parking: Only 2–4 cars can park in front of the torii gate, but there are parking meters on the road to the south.
